tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

content.content:
# Plan — `mcp.yukitools.dev` (Phase 6: MCP endpoint behind Entra)

Status: **LIVE — deployed & verified 2026-06-25.** Companion to `yukitools-sso-runbook.md`.
The browser app (`ctxlayer.yukitools.dev`) is live behind Access; the **MCP** surface at
`mcp.yukitools.dev` is now live for Entra/Yuki users. See **Implementation status** at the bottom.

## Mental model (read this first)

The OAuth flow is **already built into ctxlayer** — `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider`
gives us the whole MCP Authorization Server: dynamic client registration
(`/oauth/register`), `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/token`,
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, the bearer-gated `/mcp` transport, and
grant completion (`completeMcpAuthorization`). **We are not building an OAuth server.**

This phase is **~90% mounting + ~10% one identity bridge**:
- **Mounting:** serve the app on `mcp.yukitools.dev`, keep the machine endpoints
  public, gate only `/oauth/authorize` behind Access.
- **Bridge:** the built-in `/oauth/authorize` logs the human in via the app's own
  GitHub/Google chooser. Yuki users are **Entra** (no GitHub org / Google Workspace),
  so they can't complete it. We add **one login option** to that existing step:
  trust the Cloudflare Access JWT (Entra-via-Access). Reuses the verifier we already
  shipped. *(If MCP users could use GitHub/Google, this phase would be 100% mounting,
  zero code.)*

Cloudflare Access is the **IdP feeding identity into our OAuth server**, not the
OAuth server itself (it has no DCR / MCP discovery).

## Decision: **Option A** — reuse the Access-JWT trust on `/oauth/authorize`

One Worker, a 2nd custom domain. Minimal code, reuses everything, no new env vars,
same database as the browser app. (Option B — a generic OIDC IdP provider pointed at
Access-for-SaaS OIDC — is a larger, ~6–10h change; nice open-source addition later,
not needed for Yuki's internal MCP. See bottom.)

### Key facts that make this clean (verified 2026-06-24)
- **OAuth layer is request-host-relative.** `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is **not** passed to the
  OAuthProvider (`oauth/provider-config.ts` only sets endpoint paths). The library
  derives issuer/metadata/token-`aud` from the **request Host**. So a 2nd custom domain
  on the same Worker advertises `mcp.yukitools.dev/oauth/*` and issues host-correct
  tokens. `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` stays `ctxlayer.yukitools.dev` (only drives the browser
  app's IdP callbacks + CSRF, which Option A doesn't touch).
- **Same-origin OAuth is preserved** — all OAuth endpoints stay on `mcp.yukitools.dev`;
  we gate only the `/oauth/authorize` *path*, not a separate host.
- **MCP transport is bearer-only** (`mcp/session-do.ts` reads `this.props`; no cookies,
  no Access header). So `/mcp`, `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/register`, `/.well-known/*` are
  safe to expose publicly — they're secured by the bearer + DCR.
- **Migration `0028` already allows `idp='access'`**, and `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN` +
  `CF_ACCESS_AUD` are already set on the Worker. No new env, no schema change.

## Topology

```
Worker ctxlayer-yukitools (one deployment, one DB)
├── ctxlayer.yukitools.dev      → host-level Access app (browser SPA, gated)  ✅ live
└── mcp.yukitools.dev           → 2nd custom domain, PUBLIC by default
       /.well-known/*  /oauth/token  /oauth/register  /mcp  /sse  /cli/*  → public (bearer/DCR)
       /oauth/authorize                                                   → Access-gated (only human step)
```

**AUD reuse:** add `mcp.yukitools.dev/oauth/authorize` as a **destination on the
existing `ctxlayer.yukitools.dev` Access app** (AUD `b0dee578…`, policy "Yukitools
Eligible"). Same app ⇒ same AUD ⇒ the Worker's existing `CF_ACCESS_AUD` validates the
Access JWT from both the browser host and the MCP authorize path. No new AUD/env.

## Resulting MCP sign-in flow
1. Client → `mcp.yukitools.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (public) → AS discovery.
2. Client DCR `/oauth/register` (public), opens `/oauth/authorize?...` in a browser.
3. Access intercepts `/oauth/authorize` → Entra login → back **with `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion`**.
4. `handleAuthorize` verifies the Access JWT, upserts `idp='access'` user, calls
   `completeMcpAuthorization` → 302 to the client with the code.
5. Client exchanges code at `/oauth/token` (public) → bearer token (props userId/email/role).
6. Client calls `/mcp` (public, bearer) → `McpSessionDO` reads `ctx.props`. Done.

## Work items

### A. App change (one file, ~120 lines, generic — gated on existing `CF_ACCESS_*`)
- `apps/worker/src/oauth/authorize-page.ts` → `handleAuthorize(request, env)`: add a
  branch **before** the IdP chooser. If `accessTrustConfigured(env)` AND the
  `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` header is present → `verifyCfAccessJwt(token, env)` →
  `upsertUser({idp:'access', idpSub: id.sub, email: id.email, name: id.name, avatarUrl:null}, 'active')`
  (skip the IdP allowlist — Access already gated membership; `ADMIN_EMAILS` still sets
  role; stored `suspended`/`pending` still blocks) → store the parsed auth request in
  `OAUTH_KV` under `authReq:<requestId>` (mirror the existing path) →
  `completeMcpAuthorization(env, requestId, user)`. Fall back to the existing
  GitHub/Google chooser when no/invalid Access token (keeps the app generic).
- **Reuses (already exist):** `verifyCfAccessJwt` / `accessTrustConfigured`
  (`auth/cf-access.ts`), `upsertUser` (`db/queries/users.ts`), `completeMcpAuthorization`
  (`idp/complete-mcp.ts` — takes `(env, oauthRequestId, user: UserRow)` and calls
  `env.OAUTH_PROVIDER.completeAuthorization({request, userId, metadata, scope:['mcp'], props})`),
  `consumeAuthRequest` + `parseAuthRequest` (`oauth/authorize-page.ts`).
- **Tests:** valid Access JWT → grant completes (mock `OAUTH_PROVIDER.completeAuthorization`);
  absent/invalid token → falls back to the chooser; suspended user → blocked.

### B. Mounting (ops/Cloudflare)
1. **Add `mcp.yukitools.dev` as a 2nd custom domain** on `ctxlayer-yukitools`.
   - The shared template has ONE `[[routes]]` for `${HOST}`. Add an **optional second
     custom-domain route** gated on a new `MCP_HOST` var (empty for normal tenants),
     so `release-all` keeps it and other tenants are unaffected. Wire `MCP_HOST` through
     `provision-tenant.sh` like `HOST`/`CF_ACCESS_*`.
2. **Add `mcp.yukitools.dev/oauth/authorize` as a destination** on the existing Access
   app (look it up: `GET /accounts/<acc>/access/apps` filter `domain==ctxlayer.yukitools.dev`;
   it's AUD `b0dee578…`). Keep the "Yukitools Eligible" policy.

## Open items to verify at build time (small)
- Exact `OAUTH_PROVIDER.completeAuthorization({...})` arg shape — read `idp/complete-mcp.ts`
  in full before writing the branch.
- That `parseAuthRequest` behaves when the authorize request carries the Access
  cookie/JWT (Access just adds headers; should be transparent).
- The precise Access API field to add a 2nd destination to an existing app
  (`destinations` / `self_hosted_domains` — check current schema).
- Worker custom-domain attach for `mcp.*` coexisting with the path-scoped Access app
  (no conflict expected; the Access app sits in front of the proxied custom domain).
- MFA: if `Require: mfa` is later added to the policy, it applies to the MCP authorize
  step too — fine, but note the first MCP login then requires an MFA'd Entra session.

## Implementation status (2026-06-25)

**A. App change — DONE** (app repo `ctxlayer`, branch `feat/mcp-access-authorize`,
commit `2d2c5d4`, not yet merged). `handleAuthorize` (`oauth/authorize-page.ts`) gained
a `tryCompleteViaAccess` branch: verify `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` → `upsertUser({idp:'access'})`
→ status-guard (suspended/pending → 403 page) → `completeMcpAuthorization`; no/invalid token
falls through to the GitHub/Google chooser. 6 unit tests added; worker suite 370/370 + typecheck +
biome clean. Plan-vs-code corrections found: `upsertUser(env, input, 'active')` returns
`{ user }` (not `upsertUser({...}, 'active')`); the `complete-mcp ↔ authorize-page` import cycle
is function-level and harmless.

**B.1 Mounting — DONE** (ops repo, branch `feat/mcp-host-route`, commit `e9cc41e`).
`wrangler.template.toml` gained an optional 2nd `custom_domain` route via `${MCP_ROUTE_BLOCK}`,
rendered only when `MCP_HOST` is set. `provision-tenant.sh` accepts `MCP_HOST` and persists
`mcp_host` + `cf_access_aud` to the registry. **Bug fixed:** `release-all.sh` did not render
`CF_ACCESS_*`, so re-releasing an Access host baked literal `${CF_ACCESS_*}` into its config and

# Plan — `mcp.yukitools.dev` (Phase 6: MCP endpoint behind Entra)

Status: **LIVE — deployed & verified 2026-06-25.** Companion to `yukitools-sso-runbook.md`.
The browser app (`ctxlayer.yukitools.dev`) is live behind Access; the **MCP** surface at
`mcp.yukitools.dev` is now live for Entra/Yuki users. See **Implementation status** at the bottom.

## Mental model (read this first)

The OAuth flow is **already built into ctxlayer** — `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider`
gives us the whole MCP Authorization Server: dynamic client registration
(`/oauth/register`), `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/token`,
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, the bearer-gated `/mcp` transport, and
grant completion (`completeMcpAuthorization`). **We are not building an OAuth server.**

This phase is **~90% mounting + ~10% one identity bridge**:
- **Mounting:** serve the app on `mcp.yukitools.dev`, keep the machine endpoints
  public, gate only `/oauth/authorize` behind Access.
- **Bridge:** the built-in `/oauth/authorize` logs the human in via the app's own
  GitHub/Google chooser. Yuki users are **Entra** (no GitHub org / Google Workspace),
  so they can't complete it. We add **one login option** to that existing step:
  trust the Cloudflare Access JWT (Entra-via-Access). Reuses the verifier we already
  shipped. *(If MCP users could use GitHub/Google, this phase would be 100% mounting,
  zero code.)*

Cloudflare Access is the **IdP feeding identity into our OAuth server**, not the
OAuth server itself (it has no DCR / MCP discovery).

## Decision: **Option A** — reuse the Access-JWT trust on `/oauth/authorize`

One Worker, a 2nd custom domain. Minimal code, reuses everything, no new env vars,
same database as the browser app. (Option B — a generic OIDC IdP provider pointed at
Access-for-SaaS OIDC — is a larger, ~6–10h change; nice open-source addition later,
not needed for Yuki's internal MCP. See bottom.)

### Key facts that make this clean (verified 2026-06-24)
- **OAuth layer is request-host-relative.** `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is **not** passed to the
  OAuthProvider (`oauth/provider-config.ts` only sets endpoint paths). The library
  derives issuer/metadata/token-`aud` from the **request Host**. So a 2nd custom domain
  on the same Worker advertises `mcp.yukitools.dev/oauth/*` and issues host-correct
  tokens. `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` stays `ctxlayer.yukitools.dev` (only drives the browser
  app's IdP callbacks + CSRF, which Option A doesn't touch).
- **Same-origin OAuth is preserved** — all OAuth endpoints stay on `mcp.yukitools.dev`;
  we gate only the `/oauth/authorize` *path*, not a separate host.
- **MCP transport is bearer-only** (`mcp/session-do.ts` reads `this.props`; no cookies,
  no Access header). So `/mcp`, `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/register`, `/.well-known/*` are
  safe to expose publicly — they're secured by the bearer + DCR.
- **Migration `0028` already allows `idp='access'`**, and `CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN` +
  `CF_ACCESS_AUD` are already set on the Worker. No new env, no schema change.

## Topology

```
Worker ctxlayer-yukitools (one deployment, one DB)
├── ctxlayer.yukitools.dev      → host-level Access app (browser SPA, gated)  ✅ live
└── mcp.yukitools.dev           → 2nd custom domain, PUBLIC by default
       /.well-known/*  /oauth/token  /oauth/register  /mcp  /sse  /cli/*  → public (bearer/DCR)
       /oauth/authorize                                                   → Access-gated (only human step)
```

**AUD reuse:** add `mcp.yukitools.dev/oauth/authorize` as a **destination on the
existing `ctxlayer.yukitools.dev` Access app** (AUD `b0dee578…`, policy "Yukitools
Eligible"). Same app ⇒ same AUD ⇒ the Worker's existing `CF_ACCESS_AUD` validates the
Access JWT from both the browser host and the MCP authorize path. No new AUD/env.

## Resulting MCP sign-in flow
1. Client → `mcp.yukitools.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (public) → AS discovery.
2. Client DCR `/oauth/register` (public), opens `/oauth/authorize?...` in a browser.
3. Access intercepts `/oauth/authorize` → Entra login → back **with `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion`**.
4. `handleAuthorize` verifies the Access JWT, upserts `idp='access'` user, calls
   `completeMcpAuthorization` → 302 to the client with the code.
5. Client exchanges code at `/oauth/token` (public) → bearer token (props userId/email/role).
6. Client calls `/mcp` (public, bearer) → `McpSessionDO` reads `ctx.props`. Done.

1	/**
2	 * Nightly prune of abandoned DCR client registrations.
3	 *
4	 * MCP hosts that use RFC 8252 §7.3 loopback redirects (Claude Code,
5	 * Cursor, Windsurf, …) do a fresh Dynamic Client Registration per auth
6	 * attempt — each mints a new public `client_id` on an ephemeral
7	 * `http://localhost:<port>/callback`. Attempts that are retried,
8	 * cancelled, or superseded leave behind a registration with no grant.
9	 * `workers-oauth-provider` never expires client records, so without a
10	 * sweep these accumulate forever and clutter the admin viewer.
11	 *
12	 * Policy (see `isPrunableClient`): delete a client iff it is PUBLIC
13	 * (token_endpoint_auth_method='none'), has ZERO grants, and was
14	 * registered more than `olderThanDays` ago. Confidential clients
15	 * (stable hosted redirects, e.g. claude.ai) are never auto-pruned even
16	 * with zero grants — a missing grant there reads as "not used yet",
17	 * not "abandoned".
18	 *
19	 * Fail-closed: if the grant index is incomplete (a per-user
20	 * listUserGrants read failed, so a real grant could be invisible) we
21	 * delete NOTHING this run and report it. A legitimate client must never
22	 * be deleted because a transient KV read made it look orphaned.
23	 */
24	
25	import type { Env } from '../env'
26	import { buildUserGrantIndex, type OAuthHelpers } from './client-grants'
27	import { errMessage } from '../util/errors'
28	
29	const SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86400
30	
31	export interface PruneClientsResult {
32	  scanned: number
33	  /** Clients matching the prune policy. */
34	  orphans: number
35	  deleted: number
36	  /** deleteClient calls that threw. */
37	  failed: number
38	  /** True when we declined to delete because the grant index undercounts. */
39	  skippedIncompleteIndex: boolean
40	  deletedIds: string[]
41	}
42	
43	/** Minimal shape of a client record needed to decide prunability. */
44	interface ClientLike {
45	  clientId: string
46	  tokenEndpointAuthMethod: string
47	  registrationDate?: number | null
48	}
49	
50	/**
51	 * Pure prune predicate. `grantIndex` keys are clients that hold ≥1
52	 * grant; absence ⇒ zero grants. `cutoffSeconds` is the youngest
53	 * registration timestamp we'll still delete (older = prunable).
54	 */
55	export function isPrunableClient(
56	  client: ClientLike,
57	  grantIndex: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>,
58	  cutoffSeconds: number
59	): boolean {
60	  if (client.tokenEndpointAuthMethod !== 'none') return false // confidential
61	  if (grantIndex.has(client.clientId)) return false // has grants
62	  // No registrationDate ⇒ can't age it ⇒ keep (don't delete blind).
63	  if (typeof client.registrationDate !== 'number') return false
64	  return client.registrationDate < cutoffSeconds
65	}
66	
67	/**
68	 * Core loop, decoupled from the grant-index build so it's unit-testable
69	 * with a mock helpers + a plain Map. Paginates all clients and deletes
70	 * the prunable ones best-effort.
71	 */
72	export async function pruneClientsByPolicy(
73	  helpers: Pick<OAuthHelpers, 'listClients' | 'deleteClient'>,
74	  grantIndex: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>,
75	  cutoffSeconds: number
76	): Promise<Omit<PruneClientsResult, 'skippedIncompleteIndex'>> {
77	  let scanned = 0
78	  let orphans = 0
79	  let deleted = 0
80	  let failed = 0
81	  const deletedIds: string[] = []
82	
83	  let cursor: string | undefined
84	  let pages = 0
85	  do {
86	    const page = await helpers.listClients({ limit: 200, cursor })
87	    for (const client of page.items) {
88	      scanned++
89	      if (!isPrunableClient(client, grantIndex, cutoffSeconds)) continue
90	      orphans++
91	      try {
92	        await helpers.deleteClient(client.clientId)
93	        deleted++
94	        deletedIds.push(client.clientId)
95	      } catch (err) {
96	        failed++
97	        console.warn(
98	          `[prune-clients] deleteClient(${client.clientId}) failed:`,
99	          errMessage(err)
100	        )
101	      }
102	    }
103	    cursor = page.cursor
104	    // Safety backstop against an ill-behaved cursor — 50×200 = 10k
105	    // clients, far beyond any realistic registration count.
106	    if (++pages > 50) {
107	      console.warn('[prune-clients] stopped after 50 pages; cursor may be looping')
108	      break
109	    }
110	  } while (cursor)
111	
112	  return { scanned, orphans, deleted, failed, deletedIds }
113	}
114	
115	export async function pruneOrphanOAuthClients(
116	  env: Env,
117	  helpers: OAuthHelpers,
118	  opts: { olderThanDays: number; now?: number }
119	): Promise<PruneClientsResult> {
120	  const nowSeconds = opts.now ?? Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)
121	  const cutoff = nowSeconds - opts.olderThanDays * SECONDS_PER_DAY
122	
123	  const { index, complete } = await buildUserGrantIndex(env, helpers)
124	  if (!complete) {
125	    return {
126	      scanned: 0,
127	      orphans: 0,
128	      deleted: 0,
129	      failed: 0,
130	      skippedIncompleteIndex: true,
131	      deletedIds: []
132	    }
133	  }
134	
135	  const core = await pruneClientsByPolicy(helpers, index, cutoff)
136	  return { ...core, skippedIncompleteIndex: false }
137	}

3	 *
4	 * `index.ts` constructs the live provider; admin tooling (e.g. the
5	 * OAuth-clients viewer) constructs a read-only `OAuthHelpers` instance
6	 * via `getOAuthApi(opts, env)` and MUST use the identical KV+path
7	 * config so the helpers point at the same data the live provider
8	 * wrote. Extracted here so we can't drift.
9	 *
10	 * The `defaultHandler` is plumbed through as a parameter because
11	 * helpers paths (listClients, lookupClient, etc.) never invoke it —
12	 * admin code can pass a stub, while `index.ts` passes the real Hono
13	 * app.
14	 */

16	import type { ExportedHandler } from '@cloudflare/workers-types'
17	import type { OAuthProviderOptions } from '@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider'
18	import { McpSessionDO } from '../mcp/session-do'
19	import type { Env } from '../env'
20	
21	const NOOP_HANDLER: ExportedHandler<Env> = {
22	  fetch: () => new Response('not used by admin helpers', { status: 500 })
23	}
24	
25	export function oauthProviderOptions(
26	  defaultHandler: ExportedHandler<Env> = NOOP_HANDLER
27	): OAuthProviderOptions<Env> {
28	  // apiHandlers requires ExportedHandlerWithFetch (Required fetch);
29	  // our handlers carry `fetch` at the value level but their declared
30	  // types don't line up exactly, so the whole map is cast once.
31	  const apiHandlers = {
32	    '/mcp': McpSessionDO.serve('/mcp', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' }),
33	    '/sse': McpSessionDO.serveSSE('/sse', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' })
34	  } as OAuthProviderOptions<Env>['apiHandlers']
35	  return {
36	    apiHandlers,
37	    defaultHandler,
38	    authorizeEndpoint: '/oauth/authorize',
39	    tokenEndpoint: '/oauth/token',
40	    clientRegistrationEndpoint: '/oauth/register',
41	    scopesSupported: ['mcp']
42	  }
43	}

1	import { OAuthProvider, getOAuthApi } from '@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider'
2	import type { Env } from './env'
3	import { queueKind } from './queues/route'
4	import { app } from './app'
5	import { oauthProviderOptions } from './oauth/provider-config'
6	import { usageConsumer } from './queues/usage-consumer'
7	import { reindexConsumer } from './queues/reindex-consumer'
8	import { gitSyncConsumer } from './queues/git-sync-consumer'
9	import { jobsConsumer } from './queues/jobs-consumer'
10	import { pruneUsageEvents } from './db/queries/usage'
11	import { clearAsyncJobResults, pruneAsyncJobs } from './db/queries/async-jobs'
12	import { pruneOrphanOAuthClients } from './oauth/prune-clients'
13	import { listDueGitSyncs } from './git/sync'
14	import { audit } from './audit/log'
15	import { notify } from './ops/alert'
16	import { LAST_CRON_KV_KEY } from './ops/cron-heartbeat'
17	import { withHsts } from './util/security-headers'
18	import { isMcpPathOnWrongHost } from './util/mcp-host'
19	import { errMessage } from './util/errors'
20	import { keepWarmUserCredentials } from './upstream/keep-warm'
21	import { recordJobRun } from './ops/job-runs'
22	import { pruneJobRuns } from './db/queries/job-runs'
23	
24	export { McpSessionDO } from './mcp/session-do'
25	export { DocRoomDO } from './collab/doc-room-do'
26	
27	// Route mounting lives in `app.ts` — this module only wraps the composed
28	// Hono app in the OAuthProvider and the worker handler (HSTS + queue +
29	// scheduled).
30	
31	// OAuthProvider wraps the worker's fetch. It implements /oauth/token,
32	// /oauth/register, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, and gates
33	// /mcp + /sse on a valid bearer token. Everything else falls through
34	// to the Hono app (default handler). Provider options live in
35	// `oauth/provider-config.ts` so admin tooling can construct a
36	// read-only `OAuthHelpers` against the identical config.
37	const oauthProvider = new OAuthProvider<Env>(
38	  oauthProviderOptions({ fetch: app.fetch as ExportedHandler<Env>['fetch'] })
39	)
40	
41	const worker: ExportedHandler<Env> = {
42	  // HSTS on every worker-served response (asset responses get it from
43	  // dist/_headers — see util/security-headers.ts). Skipped on localhost so
44	  // dev doesn't pin the browser's whole `localhost` to HTTPS.
45	  fetch: async (req, env, ctx) => {
46	    // Host-scope the machine MCP surface: when a dedicated MCP host is
47	    // configured, the browser host 404s /mcp,/sse,/cli instead of answering
48	    // with a confusing `invalid_token` (a past-Access user has no MCP bearer).
49	    // No-op for single-host deployments. See util/mcp-host.ts.
50	    if (isMcpPathOnWrongHost(req, env)) {
51	      return withHsts(req, Response.json({ error: 'not_found' }, { status: 404 }))
52	    }
53	    return withHsts(req, await oauthProvider.fetch(req, env, ctx))
54	  },
55	  async queue(batch, env, ctx) {
56	    // Match on the type SUFFIX, not an exact name: queue names are
57	    // deployment-specific (tenants prefix them with the worker name, e.g.
58	    // `ctxlayer-acme-usage`). See queues/route.ts. Matching exact base
59	    // names silently broke usage/reindex/git-sync on every tenant.
60	    switch (queueKind(batch.queue)) {
61	      case 'usage':
62	        return usageConsumer(batch, env, ctx)
63	      case 'reindex':
64	        return reindexConsumer(batch, env, ctx)
65	      case 'git-sync':
66	        return gitSyncConsumer(batch, env, ctx)
67	      case 'jobs':
68	        return jobsConsumer(batch, env, ctx)
69	    }
70	    // A configured consumer with no code branch = deploy/config skew. Retry
71	    // (bounded by max_retries in wrangler.toml) rather than silently drop, and
72	    // alert so it's not invisible.
73	    console.error(`unknown queue: ${batch.queue}`)
74	    await notify(env, { level: 'error', event: 'queue.unknown', detail: String(batch.queue) })
75	    for (const msg of batch.messages) msg.retry()
76	  },
77	  async scheduled(controller, env, ctx) {
78	    // Liveness heartbeat for /api/health — any cron firing refreshes it, so a
79	    // stalled scheduler becomes visible (it otherwise emits nothing at all).
80	    ctx.waitUntil(
81	      env.OAUTH_KV.put(
82	        LAST_CRON_KV_KEY,
83	        String(Math.floor(controller.scheduledTime / 1000))
84	      ).catch((e) => console.error('[cron] heartbeat write failed', e))
85	    )
86	    // Hourly cron (`0 * * * *`): git-sync due-check. Enqueue one message per
87	    // enabled source whose sync_interval has elapsed AND that has an
88	    // unattended credential path: shared_bearer, or a user_* read strategy
89	    // with a self-designated sync identity (the message carries that userId
90	    // so the consumer resolves their stored token). See listDueGitSyncs.
91	    if (controller.cron === '0 * * * *') {
92	      ctx.waitUntil(
93	        (async () => {
94	          try {
95	            await recordJobRun(env, 'git-sync-due', async () => {
96	              const nowSec = Math.floor(controller.scheduledTime / 1000)
97	              const { due, total } = await listDueGitSyncs(env, nowSec)
98	              for (const d of due) {
99	                await env.GIT_SYNC_QUEUE.send(
100	                  d.userId ? { sourceId: d.sourceId, userId: d.userId } : { sourceId: d.sourceId }
101	                )
102	              }
103	              console.log(`[cron] git-sync: queued ${due.length}/${total} source(s)`)
104	              return { summary: { queued: due.length, total } }
105	            })
106	          } catch (err) {
107	            const m = errMessage(err)
108	            console.error(`[cron] git-sync due-check failed: ${m}`)
109	            await notify(env, { level: 'error', event: 'cron.git_sync_failed', detail: m })
110	          }
111	        })()
112	      )
113	      return
114	    }
115	
116	    // Nightly cron (`0 3 * * *`). Each task is independent and wrapped
117	    // in its own try/catch + waitUntil so a slow/failed one can't time
118	    // out the trigger or starve the others.
119	
120	    // 1. Prune raw usage_events older than 30 days (rollups stay forever).
121	    ctx.waitUntil(
122	      (async () => {
123	        try {
124	          await recordJobRun(env, 'usage-prune', async () => {
125	            const removed = await pruneUsageEvents(env, 30)
126	            console.log(`[cron] pruned ${removed} usage_events rows older than 30d`)
127	            return { summary: { removed } }
128	          })
129	        } catch (err) {
130	          const m = errMessage(err)
131	          console.error(`[cron] usage_events prune failed: ${m}`)
132	          await notify(env, { level: 'error', event: 'cron.usage_prune_failed', detail: m })
133	        }
134	      })()
135	    )
136	
137	    // 1b. async_jobs two-tier retention: drop the heavy result_json blob after
138	    // 1 day (retry-warm is 15 min; polling is a live action), but keep the
139	    // lightweight row for 30 days so the admin async-usage panel matches the
140	    // usage_events retention window, then delete.
141	    ctx.waitUntil(
142	      (async () => {
143	        try {
144	          await recordJobRun(env, 'async-retention', async () => {
145	            const cleared = await clearAsyncJobResults(env, 24 * 60 * 60)
146	            const removed = await pruneAsyncJobs(env, 30 * 24 * 60 * 60)
147	            console.log(
148	              `[cron] async_jobs: cleared ${cleared} result blobs (>1d), pruned ${removed} rows (>30d)`
149	            )
150	            return { summary: { cleared, removed } }
151	          })
152	        } catch (err) {
153	          const m = errMessage(err)
154	          console.error(`[cron] async_jobs prune failed: ${m}`)
155	          await notify(env, { level: 'error', event: 'cron.async_jobs_prune_failed', detail: m })
156	        }
157	      })()
158	    )
159	
160	    // 2. Prune abandoned DCR client registrations: public, zero-grant,
161	    // older than 1 day (the loopback-OAuth retry detritus). Fail-closed
162	    // if the grant index is incomplete — see oauth/prune-clients.ts.
163	    ctx.waitUntil(
164	      (async () => {
165	        try {
166	          await recordJobRun(env, 'oauth-client-prune', async () => {
167	            const helpers = getOAuthApi<Env>(oauthProviderOptions(), env)
168	            const r = await pruneOrphanOAuthClients(env, helpers, { olderThanDays: 1 })
169	            if (r.skippedIncompleteIndex) {
170	              console.warn('[cron] oauth-client prune skipped: grant index incomplete')
171	              return { status: 'partial' as const, summary: { skipped: 'incomplete_grant_index' } }
172	            }
173	            console.log(
174	              `[cron] pruned ${r.deleted}/${r.orphans} orphan oauth clients ` +
175	                `(scanned ${r.scanned}, ${r.failed} delete failures)`
176	            )
177	            // Same summary row the admin-initiated prune writes;
178	            // audit_log.actor_id is un-FK'd TEXT, so the sentinel is safe.
179	            if (r.deleted > 0) {
180	              await audit(env, {
181	                actorId: 'cron',
182	                action: 'oauth_client.prune',
183	                meta: {
184	                  scanned: r.scanned,
185	                  orphans: r.orphans,
186	                  deleted: r.deleted,
187	                  failed: r.failed,
188	                  deletedIds: r.deletedIds
189	                }
190	              })
191	            }
192	            return {
193	              status: r.failed > 0 ? ('partial' as const) : ('ok' as const),
194	              summary: { scanned: r.scanned, orphans: r.orphans, deleted: r.deleted, failed: r.failed }
195	            }
196	          })
197	        } catch (err) {
198	          const m = errMessage(err)
199	          console.error(`[cron] oauth-client prune failed: ${m}`)
200	          await notify(env, { level: 'error', event: 'cron.oauth_prune_failed', detail: m })
201	        }
202	      })()
203	    )
204	
205	    // 3. Keep-warm long-idle user_oauth refresh tokens so provider
206	    // inactivity windows don't silently kill them; un-preventable deaths
207	    // (scope change, revocation) surface as next-morning needsReauth
208	    // flags instead of mid-task surprises. Cadence + batch are the
209	    // rotation-spend safety knobs — see upstream/keep-warm.ts.
210	    ctx.waitUntil(
211	      (async () => {
212	        try {
213	          await recordJobRun(env, 'keep-warm', async () => {
214	            const nowSec = Math.floor(controller.scheduledTime / 1000)
215	            const r = await keepWarmUserCredentials(env, nowSec)
216	            if (r.due > 0) {
217	              console.log(`[cron] keep-warm: ${r.warmed}/${r.due} refreshed, ${r.failed} failed`)
218	            }
219	            return { status: r.failed > 0 ? ('partial' as const) : ('ok' as const), summary: r }
220	          })
221	        } catch (err) {
222	          const m = errMessage(err)
223	          console.error(`[cron] keep-warm failed: ${m}`)
224	          await notify(env, { level: 'error', event: 'cron.keep_warm_failed', detail: m })
225	        }
226	      })()
227	    )
228	
229	    // 4. Prune the job-runs ledger itself (90d) — recorded like any task.
230	    ctx.waitUntil(
231	      (async () => {
232	        try {
233	          await recordJobRun(env, 'jobs-prune', async () => {
234	            const removed = await pruneJobRuns(env, 90 * 24 * 60 * 60)
235	            return { summary: { removed } }
236	          })
237	        } catch (err) {
238	          console.error(`[cron] job-runs prune failed: ${errMessage(err)}`)
239	        }
240	      })()
241	    )
242	  }
243	}

1	/**
2	 * clientId → user-grant[] index, shared by the OAuth-clients admin
3	 * viewer (`api/admin-oauth-clients.ts`) and the orphan-client prune
4	 * (`oauth/prune-clients.ts`).
5	 *
6	 * The SDK has no inverse "grants for client" lookup, so we fan
7	 * `OAuthHelpers.listUserGrants` over every ctxlayer user in parallel
8	 * and group by `clientId`. A client absent from the returned map has
9	 * zero grants — which is exactly the signal both callers need (the
10	 * viewer renders "none"; the prune treats it as an abandoned
11	 * registration).
12	 *
13	 * Per-user failures are swallowed so one bad read can't fail the admin
14	 * page — but we surface a `complete` flag alongside the index. That
15	 * matters for the prune: a swallowed failure makes a user's real grants
16	 * LOOK like zero, which would make a legitimate client look orphaned.
17	 * The prune therefore refuses to delete anything when `complete` is
18	 * false (fail-closed); the viewer ignores the flag and shows the
19	 * best-effort index.
20	 *
21	 * Each (client, user) pair appears once; we keep the earliest
22	 * `createdAt` as `grantedAt` — the original authorisation moment, which
23	 * is what the admin cares about (refresh exchanges create new grant
24	 * rows over time).
25	 */
26	
27	import type { getOAuthApi } from '@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider'
28	import type { OAuthClientUserRef } from '@ctxlayer/shared'
29	import type { Env } from '../env'
30	import { listUserRefs } from '../db/queries/users'
31	import { errMessage } from '../util/errors'
32	
33	export type OAuthHelpers = ReturnType<typeof getOAuthApi<Env>>
34	
35	export interface UserGrantIndex {
36	  /** clientId → users who hold a grant on it. Absent key = zero grants. */
37	  index: Map<string, OAuthClientUserRef[]>
38	  /** False if any per-user listUserGrants read failed (index undercounts). */
39	  complete: boolean
40	}
41	
42	export async function buildUserGrantIndex(
43	  env: Env,
44	  helpers: OAuthHelpers
45	): Promise<UserGrantIndex> {
46	  const users = await listUserRefs(env)
47	  if (users.length === 0) return { index: new Map(), complete: true }
48	  const perUser = await Promise.all(
49	    users.map(async (u) => {
50	      try {
51	        // listUserGrants is paginated; we pull the first page only
52	        // since our scale is bounded. Promote to full pagination if
53	        // a single user ever accumulates >200 grants (unlikely).
54	        const page = await helpers.listUserGrants(u.id, { limit: 200 })
55	        return { user: u, grants: page.items, ok: true }
56	      } catch (err) {
57	        console.warn(
58	          `[client-grants] listUserGrants(${u.id}) failed:`,
59	          errMessage(err)
60	        )
61	        return { user: u, grants: [], ok: false }
62	      }
63	    })
64	  )
65	
66	  const complete = perUser.every((r) => r.ok)
67	  const index = new Map<string, OAuthClientUserRef[]>()
68	  for (const { user, grants } of perUser) {
69	    for (const g of grants) {
70	      const list = index.get(g.clientId) ?? []
71	      const existing = list.find((ref) => ref.userId === user.id)
72	      if (existing) {
73	        if (g.createdAt < existing.grantedAt) existing.grantedAt = g.createdAt
74	      } else {
75	        list.push({
76	          userId: user.id,
77	          email: user.email,
78	          name: user.name,
79	          grantedAt: g.createdAt
80	        })
81	      }
82	      index.set(g.clientId, list)
83	    }
84	  }
85	  // Stable ordering per client — earliest grant first.
86	  for (const list of index.values()) list.sort((a, b) => a.grantedAt - b.grantedAt)
87	  return { index, complete }
88	}

125	   *   1. Register every tool of any upstream connected AFTER this
126	   *      session's `init` (a mid-session connect is otherwise invisible
127	   *      until the MCP client reconnects).
128	   *   2. Reconcile ALREADY-connected upstreams against the org-global
129	   *      catalogue — the cache may have been refreshed (or healed from a
130	   *      degraded `tools/list`) by another session/admin since this
131	   *      session registered, leaving this session bound to a subset
132	   *      (2026-08-11 Datadog incident: sessions stuck on 3 of 25 tools).
133	   *      Newly-visible allowed tools are registered; nothing is ever
134	   *      unregistered mid-session (ACL revocation is backstopped in the
135	   *      call handler instead).

137	   * double-registered (registering a duplicate name would throw). Emits
138	   * `tools/list_changed` on the live server when something new registers —
139	   * a client that honors it surfaces the tools without a reconnect.
140	   * Returns a summary of what was added on either path.
141	   */

143	    server: McpServer
144	  ): Promise<{ added: { slug: string; tools: number }[]; loaded: number }> {
145	    const { rows, skillsByUpstream, docsByUpstream } = await loadUserContext(this.env, this.userId)

/**
 * A6 (2026-08 review): per-call credential freshness for user-scoped
 * upstream strategies.
 *
 * User credentials are decrypted and bound to the upstream client when the
 * MCP session initialises, so without this check a mid-session disconnect
 * (user removes the connection), admin wipe, or reauth-required flag would
 * keep working until the session dies. One D1 point-read per call makes
 * revocation bite within one call instead. The async job path re-resolves
 * the bearer from D1 at execution time, so the inline path was the only
 * stale window — but the guard runs before the async SUBMIT too, so a
 * revoked user can't queue new jobs either.
 *
 * Shared/none strategies are exempt: they are org-wide operator config,
 * not a per-user grant, and revocation there is an upstream-disable.
 */

import type { Env } from '../env'
import { getUserCredentialStatus } from '../db/queries/upstream-credentials'

export interface FreshnessConn {
  id: string
  slug: string
  authStrategy: string
}

/**
 * Returns the agent-facing error text when the user's credential for this
 * upstream is gone or flagged for re-auth, or null when the call may
 * proceed. First-party guidance (no upstream input), safe to surface.
 */
export async function credentialFreshnessError(
  env: Env,
  userId: string,
  conn: FreshnessConn
): Promise<string | null> {
  if (conn.authStrategy !== 'user_bearer' && conn.authStrategy !== 'user_oauth') return null
  const status = await getUserCredentialStatus(env, userId, conn.id)
  if (status.present && !status.needsReauth) return null
  const reason = status.present
    ? 'requires re-authorization (its token could not be refreshed)'
    : 'has been disconnected'
  return (
    `credential_revoked: your ${conn.slug} connection ${reason}. ` +
    `Reconnect it on the ctxlayer Upstreams page, then call reload_upstreams ` +
    `(or start a new session).`
  )
}

name: mcp-disconnects-2026-09-17
description: "yukitools 'daily reconnect' complaints investigated 2026-09-17: upstream grants have ABSOLUTE lifetimes (Datadog 14d, Linear ~25d, Sentry 30d, Survicate ~1d) → cohort mass-expiry → tools silently vanish; ctxlayer's own OAuth server healthy. Diagnosis only, NO code changed."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Users (Slack 2026-09-17) reported reconnecting "Yuki MCP" daily + upstreams silently failing; a colleague wrote a two-part analysis (client→gateway login vs upstream authorizations). Investigated read-only against prod; **no code changed, nothing deployed** (live = `fa0ba67`, built 2026-09-04).

**Proven (D1 audit_log + user_credentials timestamps):** upstream OAuth grants die on a fixed ABSOLUTE clock from the moment of authorization, no matter how often they are refreshed — refresh cannot extend them, so [[oauth-keepwarm-2026-08-28]] cannot prevent these:

| upstream | observed lifetime | error text |
|---|---|---|
| up-datadog | 14.1–14.8 d | RFC6749 invalid_grant boilerplate |
| up-linear | ~25.0 d (alive 24.94, dead 25.02) | `Grant not found` / `Refresh token has expired` |
| up-sentry | 30.0 d | `Grant not found` |
| up-survicate (added 2026-09-14) | ~1 d, NOT a clean absolute TTL (alive at 32h, another dead at 23h) → suspect rotation-family breakage, uninvestigated | `Invalid or expired grant` |

Linear + Sentry error strings are verbatim `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` messages → those MCP servers run the same library ctxlayer does (default `refreshTokenTTL` 30d ABSOLUTE, set at code exchange, never slid on refresh; `clientRegistrationTTL` 90d). Users onboard in cohorts → expire in cohorts (Linear cohort of 2026-08-20 died 09-14..17 = the complaint week; next cohort authorized 2026-08-24 ~10:30 UTC).

**ctxlayer's own OAuth server (Claude→gateway leg) looked healthy:** grants 3–4 weeks old still refreshing; nothing server-side kills grants (nightly `oauth-client-prune` deletes ≤5 zero-grant clients/night; `revokeAllUserGrants` is admin suspend/delete only); 0.7.0→0.10.3 upgrade did NOT change TTL defaults or refresh semantics (diffed). Re-authing users' OLD grants were still alive in KV → client side dropped/lost tokens or users re-authed by reflex when upstream tools vanished. Re-auth volume: ~2/day mid-Aug → 10–15/day week of 09-14; DCR clients 219→408 in 19 days. Unproven candidates: refresh-token rotation race (library honours only current + ONE previous RT, KV eventually consistent, 1h access TTL ⇒ hourly refresh per concurrent Claude process; morning thundering herd). **Decisive evidence = Workers Logs lines `OAuth error response: <status> <code> - <description>`** (library default `onError`).

**Code gaps found (unfixed):**
- A needsReauth/unconnected upstream registers ZERO tools in the session and nothing announces it (not in server instructions) → agent has no tools and may improvise.
- `reload_upstreams` reports `added: []` after a real 0→79 recovery: DO wake re-runs init with a fresh registry, so the diff is against in-memory state, not what the client was told. Same hibernation rule as [[skill-discovery-2026-08-26]] — persist in DO SQLite.
- `list_upstreams`: `connected: true` + `needsReauth: true` together (`connected: cred.present` in `upstreamEntry`); unconnected upstream still shows catalogue `toolsCount`.
- No upstream-401 handling on the inline call path (bearer bound at init) — but 14d of usage_events show ZERO 401-class failures, so not biting.
- A6 `credential_revoked` blocks return before `stageUsage` → invisible in the Errors table.
- keep-warm: `if (token) warmed++` counts fast-path no-ops; never-expiring creds (16× up-github + 4× up-sentry) never get `updated_at` bumped → re-selected EVERY night, permanently holding ~20 of the 25 batch slots (oldest-first) → starvation once due > 25.

**How to apply:** treat "upstream expiry is predictable" as the design lever (warn before the cliff, per-upstream learned lifetime from created_at→flag deltas) rather than more refreshing. Don't assume a gateway-side OAuth regression without the log line.

**Ops access notes:** the yukitools ops CF token (`ctxlayer-ops/.tenant-secrets/yukitools-cf.env`) CAN query D1 via REST (`POST /accounts/{acct}/d1/database/{db}/query`) and list KV keys (names + `expiration` only — grant created = expiration−30d, client registered = expiration−90d, no values needed) — works where wrangler output is dead ([[prod-reads-via-mcp]]). It CANNOT read Workers Observability (`10000 Authentication error`) — deliberate scope, don't work around; ask for the permission or have Steven run the dashboard query.

content.text:
The daily reconnects don't trace to a refresh-token regression in ctxlayer. Your upstreams' authorizations expire on a fixed clock that refreshing can't extend, and when one dies its tools drop out of the session with no warning. I changed nothing in code or prod; live is still `fa0ba67` from 2026-09-04. I used only read-only D1 SELECTs and OAuth KV key-name listing with the ops token. The ops token can't read Workers Logs (`Authentication error`), so I left those alone.

## Part 2: upstreams expire on a fixed clock

`created_at → reauth_required_at` in `user_credentials`, plus the 36 `upstream.reauth_required` audit rows of the last 3 weeks:

| upstream | lifetime from authorize | currently flagged | reason logged |
|---|---|---|---|
| up-datadog | 14.1–14.8 days | 14 of 22 | standard `invalid_grant` text |
| up-linear | about 25.0 days | 6 of 29 | `Grant not found` / `Refresh token has expired` |
| up-sentry | 30.0 days | 14 of 29 | `Grant not found` |
| up-survicate (added 09-14) | about 1 day | 4 of 5 | `Invalid or expired grant` |

- **Linear and Sentry:** their error strings are verbatim from `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider`, the library ctxlayer uses. Its refresh-token lifetime is set once at authorization and never extended by a refresh, so keep-warm can't prevent these expiries.
- **Cohorts:** users connect in batches, so they expire in batches. The Linear batch from 08-20 died 09-14 to 09-17, which is the complaint week.
- **Next Linear expiry:** 7 users authorized Linear on 08-24. On the 25-day estimate they lose it tomorrow between about 09:45 and 13:45 CEST, unless they reconnect Linear at `/app/upstreams` first.
- **Survicate** is the only upstream dying daily, and it isn't a clean fixed lifetime: one credential was alive at 32h, another dead at 23h. I suspect its refresh-token rotation is breaking. I haven't investigated that.

## Part 1: Claude → ctxlayer login

- **The server side looks healthy.** Grants 3–4 weeks old are still refreshing right now, and nothing server-side is killing logins. The nightly client prune deletes at most 5 unused registrations, and grant revocation only runs on admin suspend/delete. The August library upgrade (0.7.0 → 0.10.3) didn't change the TTL defaults or the refresh logic; I compared both.
- **Re-auths are rising.** They went from about 2/day in mid-August to 10–15/day this week, and client registrations went from 219 to 408 in 19 days. The old grants of users who re-authed are still valid on the server, so ctxlayer never revoked those logins.
- **Two causes remain possible, and I can't tell them apart:**
  - Users reconnect by reflex when upstream tools vanish. The re-auth spike lines up with the Linear die-off.
  - Concurrent Claude processes race on refresh: the library accepts only the current and one previous refresh token, and access tokens last 1 hour.
- **One check settles it:** in the Cloudflare dashboard, search the `ctxlayer-yukitools` logs for `OAuth error response` over 7 days.
  - `Invalid refresh token` means the race.
  - `Grant not found` or `expired` means ctxlayer's own 30-day login expiry.
  - No hits means users are reconnecting on their own.
- Adding Workers Observability read permission to the ops token would let me run that check myself.

## Confirmed code gaps (answers to Jan's questions)

| # | gap | where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | An upstream needing re-auth registers zero tools and nothing announces it, so the agent has no tools and may improvise. | `mcp/proxy-registry.ts`, server instructions |
| 2 | `connected: true` and `needsReauth: true` appear together, and an unconnected upstream still shows its catalogue `toolsCount`. | `mcp/catalogue-views.ts:315` |
| 3 | `reload_upstreams` reported `added: []` after a real 0 → 79 recovery. My read (not reproduced): when the session wakes it re-registers the tools before the reload handler runs, so the reload finds nothing new. The fix is to persist what the client was told, the same way the hint ledger does. | `proxy-registry.ts` `refresh()`, `session-do.ts` |
| 4 | Calls blocked for a revoked credential return before usage is recorded, so they never reach the Errors table. | `proxy-registry.ts` call handler |
| 5 | Keep-warm counts credentials that needed no refresh as "warmed". The 16 never-expiring GitHub credentials and 4 Sentry ones are re-selected every night and hold about 20 of the 25 batch slots. | `upstream/keep-warm.ts` |

Jan's "empty success" case doesn't show in the data: 14 days of proxied-call logs contain no 401 or auth-class failures. The real danger is tools going missing (gap 1), not calls failing quietly.

## What I'd build, in this order

1. Warn before expiry: learn each upstream's lifetime and show "Linear expires in 2 days" on `/app/upstreams` and in `list_upstreams`.
2. Fix gaps 1–3, keeping a dead upstream's tools listed so each call returns a hard `credential_revoked` error.
3. Fix the keep-warm batch.
4. Make ctxlayer's refresh path race-safe, only if the log check points to the race.

Tell me which of these to start on. I won't commit or deploy until you say so. The findings are saved to memory as `project_mcp_disconnects_2026-09-17.md`.

name: mcp-disconnects-2026-09-17
description: "yukitools 'daily reconnect' complaints investigated 2026-09-17: upstream grants have ABSOLUTE lifetimes (Datadog 14d, Linear ~25d, Sentry 30d, Survicate ~1d) → cohort mass-expiry → tools silently vanish; ctxlayer's own OAuth server healthy. Diagnosis only, NO code changed."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6120cbb7-0ce5-409b-a098-e5f991a03cd8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:03:09.978Z
---

Users (Slack 2026-09-17) reported reconnecting "Yuki MCP" daily + upstreams silently failing; a colleague wrote a two-part analysis (client→gateway login vs upstream authorizations). Investigated read-only against prod; **no code changed, nothing deployed** (live = `fa0ba67`, built 2026-09-04).

**Proven (D1 audit_log + user_credentials timestamps):** upstream OAuth grants die on a fixed ABSOLUTE clock from the moment of authorization, no matter how often they are refreshed — refresh cannot extend them, so [[oauth-keepwarm-2026-08-28]] cannot prevent these:

| upstream | observed lifetime | error text |
|---|---|---|
| up-datadog | 14.1–14.8 d | RFC6749 invalid_grant boilerplate |
| up-linear | ~25.0 d (alive 24.94, dead 25.02) | `Grant not found` / `Refresh token has expired` |
| up-sentry | 30.0 d | `Grant not found` |
| up-survicate (added 2026-09-14) | ~1 d, NOT a clean absolute TTL (alive at 32h, another dead at 23h) → suspect rotation-family breakage, uninvestigated | `Invalid or expired grant` |

Linear + Sentry error strings are verbatim `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` messages → those MCP servers run the same library ctxlayer does (default `refreshTokenTTL` 30d ABSOLUTE, set at code exchange, never slid on refresh; `clientRegistrationTTL` 90d). Users onboard in cohorts → expire in cohorts (Linear cohort of 2026-08-20 died 09-14..17 = the complaint week; next cohort authorized 2026-08-24 ~10:30 UTC).

**ctxlayer's own OAuth server (Claude→gateway leg) looked healthy:** grants 3–4 weeks old still refreshing; nothing server-side kills grants (nightly `oauth-client-prune` deletes ≤5 zero-grant clients/night; `revokeAllUserGrants` is admin suspend/delete only); 0.7.0→0.10.3 upgrade did NOT change TTL defaults or refresh semantics (diffed). Re-authing users' OLD grants were still alive in KV → client side dropped/lost tokens or users re-authed by reflex when upstream tools vanished. Re-auth volume: ~2/day mid-Aug → 10–15/day week of 09-14; DCR clients 219→408 in 19 days. Unproven candidates: refresh-token rotation race (library honours only current + ONE previous RT, KV eventually consistent, 1h access TTL ⇒ hourly refresh per concurrent Claude process; morning thundering herd). **Decisive evidence = Workers Logs lines `OAuth error response: <status> <code> - <description>`** (library default `onError`).

**Code gaps found (unfixed):**
- A needsReauth/unconnected upstream registers ZERO tools in the session and nothing announces it (not in server instructions) → agent has no tools and may improvise.
- `reload_upstreams` reports `added: []` after a real 0→79 recovery: DO wake re-runs init with a fresh registry, so the diff is against in-memory state, not what the client was told. Same hibernation rule as [[skill-discovery-2026-08-26]] — persist in DO SQLite.
- `list_upstreams`: `connected: true` + `needsReauth: true` together (`connected: cred.present` in `upstreamEntry`); unconnected upstream still shows catalogue `toolsCount`.
- No upstream-401 handling on the inline call path (bearer bound at init) — but 14d of usage_events show ZERO 401-class failures, so not biting.

content.text:
The screenshot confirms Part 2 (upstream expiry) and exposes a retry storm, which I've fixed in the working tree. It doesn't answer Part 1 (the Claude → ctxlayer login), because `[oauth]` is the log prefix for the upstream side only. The fix is not committed or deployed.

## What the screenshot shows

| observation | meaning |
|---|---|
| 13,650 errors in 7 days, against only 36 re-auth flags in 3 weeks | ctxlayer keeps retrying credentials it already knows are dead |
| Peak on Sep 14, about 1.2k per 2 hours | matches the day the 08-20 Linear batch expired |
| Errors come from Sentry, Datadog, Linear and Survicate, never ADO or GitHub | only upstreams that use dynamic client registration are affected |
| Blue rows: `saveTokens … expires_in=3599` | healthy refreshes are working normally |

## Cause

In `upstream/bearer.ts` the "already flagged, skip the refresh" guard existed only on the static-OAuth path (ADO, GitHub). Linear, Sentry, Datadog and Survicate use the other path, which retried the dead refresh token every time a session started or woke from idle. That produced about 2,000 failing token requests a day to third parties, all from ctxlayer's single shared client registration.

The retry made sense before the 2026-08-28 classifier change (`34f434c`), when temporary failures could also set the flag. Since then only permanent failures set it, so a retry can never recover anything.

I also found, from reading `upstream/oauth-refresh.ts`, that when two sessions of the same user refresh at once, the one that loses the single-flight lock waits 2 seconds. It then carries on with the stored, already-expired access token. It registers that upstream's tools against a token that no longer works. This is a code path for the "everything looks connected but calls fail" case Jan described. The guard removes it for flagged credentials.

## Fix (working tree only)

- **`apps/worker/src/upstream/bearer.ts`:** I moved the existing flagged-credential guard above the branch so both paths share it. It reuses the same check, so there is no new logic.
- **`apps/worker/test/integration/oauth-static-reauth.test.ts`:** I added a test for the Linear/Sentry-style path. It fails on the old code (2 outbound calls for a dead credential) and passes on the fix.
- **`bun run verify`:** passes with 667 worker unit tests, 46 web tests and 478 integration tests. The 2 lint warnings are not in the files I changed.

After deploy, the `[oauth] … auth() threw` volume should fall from about 2,000 a day to roughly one per credential per expiry. Nothing else changes for users. A flagged credential still needs the user to reconnect, and reconnecting clears the flag.

## Still open: Part 1

Run the same log view with the search text `OAuth error response` over the last 7 days. That is ctxlayer's own OAuth server logging why it rejected a Claude client.

| what shows up | meaning |
|---|---|
| `invalid_grant - Invalid refresh token` | concurrent Claude processes racing on refresh |
| `Grant not found` or `Refresh token has expired` | ctxlayer's own 30-day login expiry |
| `invalid_client` | the Claude client's registration expired |
| almost nothing | users are reconnecting by reflex when upstream tools vanish |

The 7 users who authorized Linear on 08-24 are still due to lose it tomorrow between about 09:45 and 13:45 CEST. Asking them to reconnect Linear at `/app/upstreams` in the morning avoids a repeat of Monday.

Say the word if you want this committed. The warn-before-expiry work and the three status/reload gaps from Jan's note are separate follow-ups.

content.text:
ctxlayer's own login is not failing. In that 24-hour window, 8 users re-authorized with ctxlayer, and ctxlayer had rejected at most one of them first.

## What the 5 log lines say

| line | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_grant - Invalid refresh token` | 0 | no refresh race; my theory was wrong |
| `invalid_client` | 0 | no expired or pruned client registrations |
| `invalid_grant - Grant not found` | 2 | the login no longer exists on the server |
| `invalid_token - Invalid access token` | 3 | two are the retry straight after the lines above, one is a stray |

Both `Grant not found` rejections are exact 30-day expiries. `oauth/provider-config.ts` doesn't set `refreshTokenTTL`, so the library default applies: a hard 30 days from login, never extended by use.

| client registered (UTC) | refresh rejected (UTC) |
|---|---|
| 08-18 07:34 | 09-17 08:41, the first hourly refresh after 30 days |
| 08-18 13:17 | 09-17 13:24 |

With about 50 users on several clients each, that gives a steady 2 forced re-logins a day, which is the configured behaviour, not something that broke.

## The other re-logins

The other 7 re-logins that day weren't rejected by ctxlayer. The likeliest cause is that an upstream's tools vanish and the user reconnects "Yuki MCP" by reflex. That doesn't help, because the fix is on `/app/upstreams`, and nothing tells them so.

- **One user** has had Datadog and Sentry dead since 08-10 and Linear dead since 09-16, never reconnected any of them, and re-authorized with ctxlayer on 09-15, 09-16 and 09-17. They are one of the five colleagues whose emails I matched from the Slack thread.
- **Frequent re-authorizers:** 9 of the 11 users with 3 or more ctxlayer logins since 09-07 had an upstream credential flagged since late August, and 5 still have one dead now. That is a correlation, not proof. Server data can't rule out second devices or Claude dropping tokens locally.
- **A quick way to tell:** ask Victor whether Claude shows "needs authentication", or whether the Linear and Sentry tools are simply missing.

## Recommended order

1. **Commit and deploy the retry-storm fix** from the previous turn; verify passes. It stops about 2,000 failing token requests a day to Linear, Sentry and Datadog.
2. **Make a dead upstream loud.** This is what actually removes the "daily" pain. I'd keep a flagged upstream's tools listed so every call returns the existing `credential_revoked … reconnect at /app/upstreams` error, and add an expiry warning ("Linear expires in 2 days"). This reverses part of your 08-27 "zero tools" decision, so I held off.
3. **Raise ctxlayer's login lifetime**, which is one line in `provider-config.ts`. I'd use 90 days to match the 90-day client registration lifetime. Suspending or deleting a user already revokes access instantly, so 30 days adds friction without adding safety. It only applies to new logins and would phase in over a month.
4. **Survicate dying after about 1 day** is still unexplained and needs its own look.

The 7 users who authorized Linear on 08-24 are still due to lose it tomorrow between about 09:45 and 13:45 CEST.

If you want, I'll start on item 2. Nothing is committed yet, and memory is updated.

--- release script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Roll the app repo's CURRENT checkout out to ctxlayer deployments
# (scenario B). Re-renders each per-host config from the template + registry
# (so it works on a fresh app checkout), then migrate THEN deploy.
#
# This is the ONLY upgrade path — nothing auto-upgrades. Each host keeps
# running whatever commit it was last released with (visible in the SPA
# footer / GET /api/health), so upgrades are deliberate and stageable.
#
# Usage:
#   [APP_REPO=/path/to/ctxlayer] scripts/release-all.sh                 # all hosts in tenants.json
#   scripts/release-all.sh dev stage          # only these hosts
#   scripts/release-all.sh --migrate-only     # apply migrations, skip deploy
set -euo pipefail

OPS_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
APP_REPO="${APP_REPO:-$(cd "$OPS_ROOT/../ctxlayer" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)}"
[[ -n "$APP_REPO" && -f "$APP_REPO/wrangler.toml" ]] || {
  echo "✗ APP_REPO not found (sibling ../ctxlayer). Set APP_REPO=/path/to/ctxlayer." >&2
  exit 1
}
TEMPLATE="$OPS_ROOT/wrangler.template.toml"
REGISTRY="$OPS_ROOT/tenants.json"
[ -s "$REGISTRY" ] || { echo "✗ no tenant registry at $REGISTRY." >&2; exit 1; }

# Preflight: fail fast on deploy-scheme naming drift (binding/cron parity) so a
# templated tenant can't silently lose a binding or a queue/cron consumer.
APP_REPO="$APP_REPO" "$OPS_ROOT/scripts/check-deploy-scheme.sh"

MIGRATE_ONLY=0
SELECTED=()
for a in "$@"; do
  if [[ "$a" == "--migrate-only" ]]; then MIGRATE_ONLY=1; else SELECTED+=("$a"); fi
done
if [[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  # No `mapfile`/`readarray` — macOS ships bash 3.2, where they don't exist.
  while IFS= read -r slug; do SELECTED+=("$slug"); done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' "$REGISTRY")
fi
[[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "✗ nothing to release." >&2; exit 1; }

# Cross-account guard (see docs/yukitools-provisioning.md): keep only the
# selected hosts that live in the ACTIVE Cloudflare account. The active account
# is CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID when a per-account token is exported, else the satisa
# OAuth login wrangler defaults to. A tenant's account is its registry `account`
# (entries without one predate multi-account and live in satisa). The accounts
# use different tokens that AREN'T in the registry, so deploying a tenant against
# the wrong login would create resources in the wrong account (or fail) —
# mismatched hosts are skipped here, BEFORE the build, so a wrong-creds run fails
# fast. Run release-all.sh once per account with that account's creds exported.
SATISA_ACCOUNT="${SATISA_ACCOUNT:-a65126d6fa58bfd6da28c3504b0aa859}"
ACTIVE_ACCOUNT="${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID:-$SATISA_ACCOUNT}"
DEPLOYABLE=()
for SLUG in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
  TENANT_ACCOUNT=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].account // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  TENANT_ACCOUNT="${TENANT_ACCOUNT:-$SATISA_ACCOUNT}"
  if [[ "$TENANT_ACCOUNT" != "$ACTIVE_ACCOUNT" ]]; then
    echo "⏭ $SLUG: in account $TENANT_ACCOUNT ≠ active $ACTIVE_ACCOUNT — skipping (export that account's creds to deploy it)." >&2
    continue
  fi
  DEPLOYABLE+=("$SLUG")
done
[[ ${#DEPLOYABLE[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "✗ nothing to release for account $ACTIVE_ACCOUNT — exported the right CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN/CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID?" >&2; exit 1; }

cd "$APP_REPO"
echo "▶ releasing $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) to: ${DEPLOYABLE[*]}"
bun run build:web

for SLUG in "${DEPLOYABLE[@]}"; do
  HOST=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].host // empty' "$REGISTRY")
  D1_ID=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].d1 // empty' "$REGISTRY")
  KV_ID=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].kv // empty' "$REGISTRY")
  if [[ -z "$HOST" || -z "$D1_ID" || -z "$KV_ID" ]]; then
    echo "✗ $SLUG: incomplete registry entry — skipping." >&2; continue
  fi
  # Per-host sign-in [vars]. Empty github_users → GitHub disabled unless a
  # github_org is set; a host migrated off the old secret MUST have its logins
  # recorded here (and the old ALLOWED_GITHUB_USERS secret deleted) first.
  GOOGLE_HD=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].google_hd // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  GOOGLE_EMAILS=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].google_emails // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  GITHUB_ORG=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].github_org // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  GITHUB_USERS=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].github_users // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  GATEWAY_ALIAS=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].gateway_alias // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  # Cloudflare Access trust ([vars]; non-secret) + the optional 2nd custom
  # domain. These MUST be re-rendered here too — the template references them, so
  # omitting them would bake literal ${CF_ACCESS_*}/${MCP_ROUTE_BLOCK} into the
  # config and break Access on the host. Empty for non-Access / single-domain
  # tenants. AUD is config, not a secret, so it lives in the registry.
  CF_ACCESS_TEAM=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].cf_access_team // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  CF_ACCESS_AUD=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].cf_access_aud // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  MCP_HOST=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].mcp_host // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  MCP_ROUTE_BLOCK=""
  MCP_PUBLIC_URL=""
  if [[ -n "$MCP_HOST" ]]; then
    MCP_ROUTE_BLOCK=$(printf '[[routes]]\npattern = "%s"\ncustom_domain = true' "$MCP_HOST")
    MCP_PUBLIC_URL="https://$MCP_HOST"   # drives the app's MCP-setup page URL
  fi
  WORKER="ctxlayer-${SLUG}"
  CFG="wrangler.${SLUG}.toml"
  echo "── $SLUG ($HOST)${MCP_HOST:+ +$MCP_HOST}${CF_ACCESS_TEAM:+ [access]} ──"
  WORKER="$WORKER" HOST="$HOST" D1_ID="$D1_ID" KV_ID="$KV_ID" \
  ALLOWED_GOOGLE_HD="$GOOGLE_HD" ALLOWED_GOOGLE_EMAILS="$GOOGLE_EMAILS" \
  ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORG="$GITHUB_ORG" ALLOWED_GITHUB_USERS="$GITHUB_USERS" \
  CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN="$CF_ACCESS_TEAM" CF_ACCESS_AUD="$CF_ACCESS_AUD" \
  MCP_ROUTE_BLOCK="$MCP_ROUTE_BLOCK" MCP_PUBLIC_URL="$MCP_PUBLIC_URL" \
  GATEWAY_ALIAS="$GATEWAY_ALIAS" \
    envsubst '${WORKER} ${HOST} ${D1_ID} ${KV_ID} ${ALLOWED_GOOGLE_HD} ${ALLOWED_GOOGLE_EMAILS} ${ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORG} ${ALLOWED_GITHUB_USERS} ${CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN} ${CF_ACCESS_AUD} ${MCP_ROUTE_BLOCK} ${MCP_PUBLIC_URL} ${GATEWAY_ALIAS}' \
    < "$TEMPLATE" > "$APP_REPO/$CFG"
  wrangler d1 migrations apply "$WORKER" --remote -c "$CFG"
  if [[ "$MIGRATE_ONLY" -eq 0 ]]; then
    PUBLIC_BASE_URL="https://${HOST}" bun scripts/deploy.mjs --config "$CFG"
    # Access-gated hosts answer /api/health with a 302 to the team login, not a
    # JSON body — treat 200 (open / bypass) or 302 (Access enforcing) as healthy.
    code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://${HOST}/api/health" || true)
    case "$code" in
      200) curl -fsS "https://${HOST}/api/health" | jq -e '.ok' >/dev/null && echo "✓ $SLUG" ;;
      302) echo "✓ $SLUG (Access enforcing, HTTP 302)" ;;
      *)   echo "⚠ $SLUG: /api/health returned HTTP $code" >&2 ;;
    esac
  fi
done
echo "✅ release complete."

import { createExecutionContext, env, waitOnExecutionContext } from 'cloudflare:test'

/**

 * `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` — PKCE enforcement, redirect_uri
 * matching, authorization-code single-use. The 2026-07 review flagged them
 * as delegated-and-unverifiable (the library is not vendored, so nothing
 * in-repo asserted them). These tests run the real provider against real
 * KV in workerd, so a library upgrade that regresses any of them fails CI
 * instead of shipping.

 * parseAuthRequest/completeAuthorization helper pair the IdP callback
 * bridge uses (idp/complete-mcp.ts), and codes are exchanged at the real
 * /oauth/token endpoint.
 */

const BASE = 'https://ctxlayer-oauth-sec.test'
const REDIRECT = 'https://client.example/callback'
const OTHER_REDIRECT = 'https://evil.example/steal'

const testEnv = env as unknown as WorkerEnv

// Stub default handler: these tests only exercise the provider's own
// endpoints, so the fallthrough should never be reached.
const provider = new OAuthProvider<WorkerEnv>(
  oauthProviderOptions({
    fetch: () => Promise.resolve(new Response('unexpected fallthrough', { status: 500 }))
  })
)

async function pfetch(input: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response> {
  const ctx = createExecutionContext()
  const res = await provider.fetch(new Request(input, init), testEnv, ctx)
  await waitOnExecutionContext(ctx)
  return res
}

async function registerPublicClient(): Promise<string> {
  const res = await pfetch(`${BASE}/oauth/register`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      client_name: 'sec-test-client',
      redirect_uris: [REDIRECT],
      token_endpoint_auth_method: 'none',
      grant_types: ['authorization_code', 'refresh_token'],
      response_types: ['code']
    })
  })
  expect(res.status).toBe(201)
  const body = (await res.json()) as { client_id: string }
  return body.client_id
}

/**
 * Single source of truth for the OAuthProvider config.
 *
 * `index.ts` constructs the live provider; admin tooling (e.g. the
 * OAuth-clients viewer) constructs a read-only `OAuthHelpers` instance
 * via `getOAuthApi(opts, env)` and MUST use the identical KV+path
 * config so the helpers point at the same data the live provider
 * wrote. Extracted here so we can't drift.
 *
 * The `defaultHandler` is plumbed through as a parameter because
 * helpers paths (listClients, lookupClient, etc.) never invoke it —
 * admin code can pass a stub, while `index.ts` passes the real Hono
 * app.
 */

import type { ExportedHandler } from '@cloudflare/workers-types'
import type { OAuthProviderOptions } from '@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider'
import { McpSessionDO } from '../mcp/session-do'
import type { Env } from '../env'

const NOOP_HANDLER: ExportedHandler<Env> = {
  fetch: () => new Response('not used by admin helpers', { status: 500 })
}

/**
 * How long an MCP client's login lasts before the user must re-authorize.
 * The library stamps this ONCE at the authorization-code exchange and never
 * slides it on refresh — it is an absolute lifetime, not an idle timeout. The
 * library default (30 days) forced every client of every user through a
 * monthly re-login for no security gain: suspend/delete already revoke all
 * of a user's grants instantly (oauth/revoke-grants.ts) and the session DO
 * re-checks user status on init. 90 days matches the library's DCR client
 * registration lifetime (`clientRegistrationTTL` default), which caps a
 * login anyway — a client record that expires first just turns the final
 * refresh into `invalid_client` instead of `invalid_grant`; both mean
 * "log in again". Applies to NEW logins only: existing grants keep the
 * expiry they were issued with.
 */
export const MCP_LOGIN_TTL_SECONDS = 90 * 24 * 60 * 60

export function oauthProviderOptions(
  defaultHandler: ExportedHandler<Env> = NOOP_HANDLER
): OAuthProviderOptions<Env> {
  // apiHandlers requires ExportedHandlerWithFetch (Required fetch);
  // our handlers carry `fetch` at the value level but their declared
  // types don't line up exactly, so the whole map is cast once.
  const apiHandlers = {
    '/mcp': McpSessionDO.serve('/mcp', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' }),
    '/sse': McpSessionDO.serveSSE('/sse', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' })
  } as OAuthProviderOptions<Env>['apiHandlers']
  return {
    apiHandlers,
    defaultHandler,
    authorizeEndpoint: '/oauth/authorize',
    tokenEndpoint: '/oauth/token',
    clientRegistrationEndpoint: '/oauth/register',
    scopesSupported: ['mcp']
  }
}

 * monthly re-login on every client (2026-09-17 yukitools finding: both of a
 * day's rejected refreshes were exact 30-day expiries). Pinned here so a
 * dropped option — or a library default change — fails CI instead of
 * silently shortening everyone's login.
 */
describe('MCP login lifetime (refreshTokenTTL)', () => {
  it('a new login expires MCP_LOGIN_TTL_SECONDS (90d) after the code exchange', async () => {
    expect(MCP_LOGIN_TTL_SECONDS).toBe(90 * 24 * 60 * 60)
    const clientId = await registerPublicClient()
    const verifier = 'sec-test-verifier-ttl-0123456789-0123456789-0123'
    const code = await issueCode(clientId, { challenge: await s256(verifier) })
    const before = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)
    expect((await exchange(clientId, code, { verifier })).status).toBe(200)

    const helpers = getOAuthApi<WorkerEnv>(oauthProviderOptions(), testEnv)
    const grants = (await helpers.listUserGrants('u-sec')).items.filter((g) => g.clientId === clientId)
    expect(grants).toHaveLength(1)
    const expiresAt = grants[0]?.expiresAt ?? 0
    expect(expiresAt).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(before + MCP_LOGIN_TTL_SECONDS)
    expect(expiresAt).toBeLessThanOrEqual(before + MCP_LOGIN_TTL_SECONDS + 60)
  })
})

-- When the CURRENT upstream grant was issued — i.e. the last interactive
-- authorization (OAuth code exchange), not the last token refresh.
--
-- Several upstream MCP servers give a grant a fixed ABSOLUTE lifetime from
-- the moment of authorization that no amount of refreshing extends (field
-- finding 2026-09-17: Datadog 14d, Linear ~25d, Sentry 30d). With this
-- stamp plus the admin-configured `authConfig.grantLifetimeDays`, ctxlayer
-- can warn BEFORE the cliff instead of discovering the death at the next
-- refresh. `created_at` can't carry this: the upsert keeps it across a
-- re-authorization that reuses the row, and `updated_at` moves on every
-- refresh.
--
-- Backfill from `created_at`: until now every interactive re-auth went
-- through a DELETE + INSERT of the row (Disconnect, or the wipe-and-retry
-- in api/upstream-oauth.ts), so for existing rows the two coincide.
-- Additive nullable column on a child table — no rebuild (G1 not in play).
ALTER TABLE user_credentials ADD COLUMN granted_at INTEGER;
UPDATE user_credentials SET granted_at = created_at WHERE granted_at IS NULL;

2	 * Per-session registry that hydrates proxied upstream tools onto the
3	 * `McpServer` alongside the built-ins.
4	 *
5	 * Lifecycle:
6	 *   - `init(server)` runs once per session in `McpSessionDO.init()`.
7	 *     It enumerates upstreams the caller can reach (visibility +
8	 *     credentials), decrypts each bearer, ensures the catalogue cache
9	 *     is fresh, and registers one mangled MCP tool per cached
10	 *     `upstream_tools` row.
11	 *   - Tool handlers dispatch through the cached `UpstreamClient` via
12	 *     `upstream-call-runner.ts`, or through `async-submit.ts` for
13	 *     tools on the upstream's `authConfig.asyncTools`.
14	 *   - There is no teardown: sessions are short-lived and the workerd
15	 *     isolate frees Client state on its own when the DO dies.
16	 *
17	 * Catalogue freshness: a row older than `CATALOGUE_TTL_SECONDS` is
18	 * refreshed inline on first session encounter — accepted as a one-time
19	 * connect cost so the agent sees a complete `tools/list` immediately.
20	 * Empty cache (brand-new upstream) is also refreshed inline.
21	 *
22	 * The read-models behind `describe_upstream` / `list_upstreams` /
23	 * `restrictedTools` live in `catalogue-views.ts`.
24	 */
